subject: LynxMed private cluster: capacity squeeze, rising 5xx and p95 — immediate mitigation plan
messages:
From: Elliot Stone <elliot.stone@lynxmed.com>

Cc: SreTeamOps <sre@lynxmed.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: p95 latency + 502s spike in private cluster

Laura —

We started seeing a sharp rise in p95 latency across our private cluster after the 03:00 deploy window. Error rate (502/504) climbed from ~0.2% to 3.4% and sustained throughput dropped ~22%. This is affecting live inference traffic for our triage workflow.

We opened a ticket to your monitoring link (INF-4821). Our SREs suspect a runtime mismatch after the quantized model rollout yesterday (we rolled to q4_8). Can we get an immediate rollback or throttled fallback to the hosted variant? SLA impact is material — we may need exec attention if not resolved in the next 90 minutes.

Attached a condensed log bundle and sample traces.

—Elliot
Elliot Stone

Elliot — thanks for the quick alert and the logs. We see the same spike on our side and I’ve opened an incident (INF-4821) and pulled the on-call infra lead in.

Immediate plan (first 60 mins):
- Route new inference traffic for the critical triage route to Redwood hosted fallback (will not remove data residency, we will proxy only inference tokens).
- Start emergency rollback to previous non-quantized model build on the affected VPC nodes.
- Warm KV cache on a small canary subset to avoid coldstart amplification.

Can you confirm whether you triggered any autoscale limits or node drains during your 03:00 window? I’ll coordinate a short war room and follow up with timelines.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:26:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Production: p95 latency + 502s spike in private cluster

Laura / team —

Quick triage from the runtime side: preliminary stack traces in the attached logs show a sustained decoder kernel fallback loop on nodes with the q4_8 quantized library. We’re seeing a KV cache miss storm (hot prefixes) that causes repeated offloads and increases end-to-end latency. Two immediate mitigations I recommend now:

1) Roll back to model build v20261028-nq (non-quantized) on the affected subset and keep a small canary of q4_8 pinned for investigation.
2) Apply a temporary prefix-caching policy: pin top-200 prefixes to local RAM on the node group; raise batch_max to 16 for those routes to reduce per-token overhead.

I’ll prepare the rollback runbook; Marissa can you coordinate the rollback window with LynxMed SRE and verify we have snapshot backups of their current shard configs?

—Markus
Markus Klein

Subject: Re: Production: p95 latency + 502s spike in private cluster — incident update and exec brief

Elliot —

Rollback completed at 08:18 PST. Traffic diversion (30% to hosted fallback) was in place during the window. Key outcomes:
- p95 latency for the triage route dropped from 1.9s -> 0.42s within two warmup cycles.
- 5xx error rate returned to baseline (~0.25%) after cache heat and rollback.
- Throughput recovered to within 98% of baseline; we kept a 5% buffer for the next 24h.

Actions & next steps (for execs / account owners):
- Postmortem in 48 hours (INF-4821) with root cause analysis: quantized kernel fallback loop + KV cache misheat on high prefix variance.
- We recommend rolling forward a patched q4_8 build that includes kernel guardrails and adaptive prefix-hinting; target patch release: 20261112.
- Planning a joint run of a full warmup script for all private clusters before any quantized rollouts.

If you want an executive sync, I can get Markus and Jonas on a 15-min CTO-level update this afternoon. Please let me know.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
